reason: Partial refutation. The facts in R11S-8 check out, but it claims more than it shows and understates the R8 conflict. Verified: (a) round7/REPORT.md l.95 and CONTEXT P6 (l.2144) reject 'successor + insertion' in the words quoted. (b) The insertion read +0.001 public twice: #35 0.954 vs #34 0.953 (CONTEXT l.1797/1801), #37 0.954 vs #38 0.953; lab +0.0058 / +0.0065. (c) I re-ran scratchpad/transplant_probe.py: on amanatar old, amanatar v10 and HF v3 the changed cells are [4,5] with the same hunks and the same new cells, and the FINAL print still follows /divinsert. Problems: (1) Objection 1 is not 'answered', only shown feasible. tools/build_probe_kernel.py still has no succ base and no --base-ipynb (only BASES at l.105). The fix is a design (R11S-4), not code. (2) R8 and the round's HARD LINE ask for 'submittable by 27 Sep 12:00 with an honest lab gate, a dummy and a new OK'. An SI on a successor that does not exist yet cannot be submitted by R8. An HF v3 proxy dummy tests the tooling, not the file that would be submitted. The real SI dummy would run after the trigger, so after R8. (3) R11S-8 admits there is no lab gate and calls it 'mitigated' by keeping #37 and by R1's public(SI) >= public(PORT). Under R8 a mitigation is not a gate. SI is admissible only if the user explicitly amends R8/P6 and accepts a named substitute gate ('transfer by construction, not measured on S'), as scan_plancheck PC11-03/PC11-12 say. R11S-8 should say this plainly and not imply that tooling plus a proxy dummy is enough. (4) R11S-8 leaves out a clause the transfer argument depends on: the successor's diff must not touch the division stages (PC11-11(3)/PC11-12(b)). (5) Round 11 has not settled which recipe to use. R11S-4/R11S-8 use K2 (lowrefine on). PC11-07 argues for K1, because tools/dummy_gates.py --k2 hard-codes x138 constants (l.112, raw nodes == 121,777) and lowrefine's private prior is ~0. (6) Value is small. By R11S-2's own Monte Carlo, an early verbatim port beats SI for bronze (0.84 vs 0.80 at s=0.954). SI wins only on late detection or silver, and P(trigger) is ~0.10-0.15. These numbers are priors, and the 'second ticket' effect inflates them. The OC line is not re-proposed and no closed idea is revived, so this is not a closed line in disguise.
fix: Restate R11S-8 as follows. Round 7's rejection of SI STANDS under R8/P6 as written. It can be lifted only by ONE explicit user amendment before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC (logged with date -u, before any trigger) that: (i) replaces P6's last sentence; (ii) names the substitute gate as 'transfer by construction, not measured on S'. That gate is: code identity against the x138 -> recipe hunks, the successor's diff = 1-2 mechanisms that do not touch the division stages, the SI dummy gates G1-G7 on the real SI file, and the public read table with #37 in every pair; (iii) is backed by builder code, tests and a byte-identical finals rebuild (exp58 1f1ddb6d / exp58t a77bcd6b / exp58n 55038fd6) committed before R8, with HF v3 proxy dummies as a tooling test only. Pick ONE recipe (K1 per PC11-07, or K2 with PORT-relative gates per R11S-4) before asking. If there is no OK by R8, record 'SI unavailable; port-only E10 v2 at the agreed threshold'. Curator: I-026/I-256 -> 'E10 v2 proposed (round 11), SI conditional on explicit R8 amendment'. For I-262, keep the existing 'covered by I-281' note and add 'trigger-to-submit timing still unmeasured'.
realistic_gain: Close to zero for the recheck itself (bookkeeping). SI over a port-only v2: about 0 to +0.02 P(bronze), and about +0.01 P(silver), in expectation over P(trigger) ~0.10-0.15. These are model priors, not measurements, and SI is worse than an early port for bronze. No effect in the ~85-90% of worlds with no successor.
